correctness.rationale: For every r>0, 0<a<1, 0<q<min(a,1-a), t>0, the cubic-flow variational identity gives Phi_t''/Phi_t' = r(int_0^t Phi_s' ds)[2(1+a)-3(x+Phi_t(x))]. The integral is strictly positive; x+Phi_t(x) is strictly increasing from 0 to 2, so Phi_t' has one strict maximum. Its sliding-window integral Phi_t(x+q)-Phi_t(x) is strictly unimodal. The difference from q is negative at 0 and 1-q, positive at a-q and a, forcing exactly two simple equality roots with the claimed ordering. The normalized non-overstocking domain follows from inverse monotonicity. Uniform small-time expansion gives two explicit simple quadratic roots; convergence to the two Allee basin attractors yields long-time limits. The symbolic cubic derivative and 96 randomized numerically integrated parameter cases plus exactly soluble symmetric example were independently checked. The universal proof does not depend on numerical tests.

evidence: For a scalar autonomous ODE, order preservation alone gives Phi_t increasing, but does not imply uniqueness of finite-difference crossings. The new proof uses the special exact factorization of the cubic derivative and the sign of Phi_t''.

originality.rationale: Exact all-horizon two-switch classification is not stated in the materially examined 2008 continuous augmentation study or 2012 discrete augmentation ordering study. Searches for exact finite-dose cubic Allee pulse comparison, density thresholds and broader S-shaped-flow implications did not identify a covering theorem. This is a best-knowledge literature assessment, not proof of historical uniqueness. The key difference from prior work is global quantification over all initial densities, all r>0, all t>0 and the whole stated q-range, rather than a characterization of optimal controls or selected numerical scenarios.

value.rationale: Species augmentation is used to rescue small Allee-limited populations (2008 and 2012 population-augmentation studies). Exact finite-horizon choice between equally costly beginning and end releases is a natural decision problem. The theorem gives a complete two-threshold classification for the full a,r,t domain under the ecologically meaningful pulse bound, not an arbitrary one-off parameter case. It proves that neither universally earlier nor universally later stocking is optimal and identifies a shrinking Allee-crossing interval as the horizon lengthens; both crossings remain in a terminal carrying-capacity-feasible region. The derivative-shape structural lemma and short/long-time boundaries give a useful analytical benchmark for more involved conservation controls.
